Fact.Name: Return files Form 8938
Fact.Description: True only when the return has answered the Form 8938 threshold question and its complete-safe threshold result is above the applicable reporting limit. The answer guard distinguishes an unasked return from an answered below-threshold return.

Fact.Name: Knockout: this return must attach Form 8938
Fact.Description: Your specified foreign financial assets are above the Form 8938 reporting threshold that applies to you, so Form 8938 must be attached to this return. This service cannot prepare a complete Form 8938 yet, so this return cannot be filed here.

Fact.Name: The finished Part V and Part VI rows add up to more than the total the filer stated for the last day of the year
Fact.Description: TRUE when the answered last-day total of all specified foreign financial assets is smaller than the sum of the year-end values of the assets entered row by row. The rows are a subset of all the filer's assets, so their sum can never honestly exceed the stated total. FALSE when the stated total is unanswered or at least the row sum. Read only beside /form8938ComputedInventoryComplete.

Fact.Name: A single entered asset's maximum value is more than the total the filer stated for any time during the year
Fact.Description: TRUE when the answered any-time total of all specified foreign financial assets is smaller than the maximum value of one single asset entered in Part V or Part VI. The total at any time includes that asset at its highest value, so no one asset can honestly exceed it. Individual maximums are compared one at a time, never summed, because different assets can peak at different times. FALSE when the stated total is unanswered or when no single row exceeds it. Read only beside /form8938ComputedInventoryComplete.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the stated Form 8938 totals are smaller than the assets entered
Fact.Description: The total value you stated for your specified foreign financial assets is smaller than the assets you listed one by one: either the listed year-end values add up to more than your stated year-end total, or one listed asset's maximum value is more than your stated total for any time during the year. Correct the stated totals or the listed assets before filing.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 threshold input: total value of specified foreign financial assets on the last day of the tax year
Fact.Description: The total value, in U.S. dollars, of every specified foreign financial asset in which the filer (and, on a joint return, the spouse) has an interest, measured on the LAST DAY of the tax year. This is the first of the two figures the Form 8938 reporting threshold is tested against; the second is the maximum at any time during the year. A SPECIFIED FOREIGN FINANCIAL ASSET is a financial account maintained by a foreign financial institution, or, when not held in an account at a financial institution, stock or securities of a non-U.S. issuer, a financial instrument or contract with a non-U.S. issuer or counterparty, or an interest in a foreign entity (IRC 6038D(b)). THE FILER APPLIES THE PRINTED VALUATION RULES BEFORE ENTERING THIS FIGURE, and the Instructions state them: fair market value, foreign currency converted to U.S. dollars; an asset with no positive value counts as zero; a jointly owned asset is counted ONCE at its entire value on a joint return, at ONE-HALF of its value when the co-owner is a spouse who files separately and is a specified individual, and at its entire value when the co-owner is anyone else; a SPECIFIED INDIVIDUAL INCLUDES the value of every specified foreign financial asset EVEN WHEN it is reported on another form listed in Part IV (Forms 3520, 3520-A, 5471, 8621 and 8865) - those assets are excepted from Form 8938 Part IV's own detail reporting, not from this threshold total; only a SPECIFIED DOMESTIC ENTITY leaves them out, and every return this dictionary builds is a specified individual's. TWO CLASSES OF ASSET ARE LEFT OUT of the total, and the same Determining the Total Value section is where the Instructions say so: (1) specified foreign financial assets the filer is not required to report because he is a BONA FIDE RESIDENT OF A U.S. POSSESSION (i8938 lines 330-338: "Do not include the value of specified" "foreign financial assets you are not" "required to report because you are a" "bona fide resident of a U.S." "possession."), and (2) assets the filer is not required to report because he is an OWNER OF A DOMESTIC WIDELY HELD FIXED INVESTMENT TRUST or of a domestic liquidating trust created under chapter 7 or chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code (i8938 lines 342-354). IRC 6038D(h)(1) and (h)(3) are the authority for both carve-outs. Neither is computed here, and neither can be: which of the filer's assets fall in those classes is not a quantity this dictionary holds, so the exclusion is the filer's own application of the printed rules, exactly like the fair-market-value and joint-ownership rules above. /isBonaFidePuertoRicoResident (ctcOdc.xml) knows the possession answer for Schedule 8812 and is DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED to these aggregates: it would take a per-asset possession flag on a Part V/VI row, and the aggregates are attested, not derived. Those rules are the filer's own application; the two aggregates here are attested directly rather than derived from a per-asset collection. The two aggregates here are still attested rather than derived from it: they are the return-level "total value" and "maximum value" figures the threshold test reads directly, and deriving them from the Part V/VI collections would need Part VI (other assets) built first, or the derived figure under-states a return that also holds other-asset items. Optional: unanswered means the aggregate was not asked, and the return-level answer then falls back to the filer's yes/no attestation or, failing that, is treated as UNANSWERED, which every reading guard refuses.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 threshold input: maximum total value of specified foreign financial assets at any time during the tax year
Fact.Description: The highest total value, in U.S. dollars, that the filer's specified foreign financial assets reached AT ANY TIME during the tax year, valued under the same printed rules as the last-day figure (see /writableForm8938TotalValueOnLastDayOfYear). It is the second operand of the two-figure threshold test and it is what makes an asset sold before year end still count: the Instructions' Example 3 has a last-day total of $0 and a maximum of $125,000 and concludes "You have to file Form 8938". The statute itself asks for "the maximum value of the asset during the taxable year" (IRC 6038D(c)(4)), which is why the year-round figure is a distinct intake and not derived from the last-day one. Optional: unanswered means the aggregate was not asked; both aggregates must be answered before the computed arm of /form8938AboveReportingThreshold is taken.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 residence fork: tax home in a foreign country and a presence-abroad test met
Fact.Description: Whether the filer is a taxpayer LIVING OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES for Form 8938 purposes, which quadruples every threshold figure. The Instructions make this two conditions, both of which must hold: (1) the filer's TAX HOME is in a foreign country, and (2) the filer meets ONE of the two presence-abroad tests: (a) a U.S. citizen who has been a bona fide resident of a foreign country or countries for an uninterrupted period that includes an entire tax year, or (b) a U.S. citizen or resident who is present in a foreign country or countries at least 330 full days during any period of 12 consecutive months that ENDS in the tax year being reported. ONE ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION, and the reuse that was considered and rejected is named: form2555 ships the Form 2555 line 10 bona-fide-residence began and ended dates, the line 16 physical-presence period began and ended dates and the hand-typed line 18 full-day counts (form2555.xml, the writableForm2555Line10BonaFideResidence... and ...Line16PhysicalPresencePeriod... facts), but no shipping fact anywhere resolves either test to a yes or no, the 12-month window under IRC 911(d)(1)(B) is not required to end in the tax year while this test's is, and a Form 2555 is per filer while this question is put to the return. So the quantity is not the same and the answer is the filer's own. DIRECTION WHEN UNANSWERED: /form8938LivesAbroad reads FALSE, which selects the LOWER, in-the-United-States pair; a filer who actually lives abroad and did not answer is therefore tested against a threshold up to four times too low, which can only produce a refusal (a Form 8938 owed that this dictionary does not produce), never a filed return that omitted one.

Fact.Name: Lives abroad for Form 8938 purposes (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The residence-fork answer read complete safely: the filer's attestation when given, FALSE when it was not. FALSE selects the in-the-United-States threshold pair, the lower one, so an unanswered fork can only over-refuse and never under-report; the direction is argued on the writable.

Fact.Name: The spouse is a specified individual
Fact.Description: Whether the filer's spouse is himself or herself a specified individual: a U.S. citizen, a resident alien of the United States for any part of the tax year, a nonresident alien who elects to be treated as a resident alien to file a joint return, or a nonresident alien who is a bona fide resident of American Samoa or Puerto Rico. It is a status, not a filing duty: the answer is yes even when the spouse does not have to file Form 8938. THE ONE THING THIS ANSWER DECIDES is whether an asset held jointly with the spouse enters THIS return's reporting-threshold total at one-half or in full, on a return that is married filing separately. Two specified individuals filing separate annual returns each include one-half of the jointly owned value; a joint owner whose spouse is not a specified individual includes the entire value. It changes nothing on any other filing status, nothing on the printed statement, and nothing about what any single asset is worth. Optional: unanswered leaves every jointly owned row at its full value, which can only make the return owe the form, never excuse it. This is also the only place this module touches the specified-person question at all; whether the FILER is a specified individual is still assumed rather than modelled, and that assumption is named in the Form 8938 contract.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 reporting threshold: the last-day-of-year figure that applies to this return
Fact.Description: The "more than ... on the last day of the tax year" figure from the Instructions' threshold table for specified individuals, selected by filing status and by the residence fork. FOUR CELLS, not six: married filing jointly in the United States $100,000; married filing jointly abroad $400,000; every other status in the United States $50,000; every other status abroad $200,000. The unmarried and married-filing-separately paragraphs print the same figure in each residence cell, so head of household and qualifying surviving spouse take the not-joint figure whichever paragraph a reader files them under. The test is STRICT: a total equal to the figure does not satisfy it. Incomplete until the filing status is known; the return-level answer gates on that before reading this fact. Every figure is a ledger parameter (authority/ty2025/parameters.tsv) anchored to the printed line.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 reporting threshold: the at-any-time-during-the-year figure that applies to this return
Fact.Description: The "or more than ... at any time during the tax year" figure from the same table, selected the same way: married filing jointly in the United States $150,000; married filing jointly abroad $600,000; every other status in the United States $75,000; every other status abroad $300,000. THE ABROAD MARRIED-FILING-SEPARATELY FIGURE is read here from the vendored file itself: its sentence runs down the middle column of page 4 to "$200,000 on the last day of the tax" (line 322) and continues at the head of the right column of the same page, "year or more than $300,000 at any" / "time during the tax year." (lines 245-246); a reading-order re-extraction of the page confirms the join. It equals the unmarried-abroad figure, as the last-day halves do. Strict test, ledger parameters, Incomplete until the filing status is known, all as on the last-day twin.

Fact.Name: Both Form 8938 asset aggregates and the filing status are answered
Fact.Description: The answered-ness predicate for the COMPUTED arm of the return-level threshold answer: TRUE only when the last-day total, the maximum-during-the-year total AND the filing status are all answered. All three are needed because the test has two operands and the table is keyed on the status; a single answered aggregate proves nothing about the other arm. Built from IsComplete on the leaves only, never on a complete-safe fact beside it. A return that never answers either aggregate is also answered when its own Part V and Part VI rows are finished and valued and the filing status is known (/form8938ComputedInventoryComplete), because the rows then supply both operands. The attested figures keep their precedence inside /form8938EffectiveLastDayValue and /form8938EffectiveMaximumValue; this fact only says that SOME route has an answer. Adding the route can move a return from unanswered to answered, which is the point: an answered below-threshold return stops being refused by the three guards that read the pair.

Fact.Name: The Form 8938 threshold question has an answer on this return
Fact.Description: Whether the return can say, either way, if it is above the Form 8938 reporting threshold: TRUE when the computed arm's inputs are answered (/form8938AggregatesAnswered) OR when the filer answered the yes/no attestation form1099Rs:/writableSpecifiedForeignFinancialAssetsAboveForm8938Threshold. THIS IS THE HALF OF THE PAIR THAT MAKES THE OTHER HALF SAFE TO READ. /form8938AboveReportingThreshold is complete safe and resolves FALSE when nothing was answered; a guard reading it alone would treat a never-asked filer as below threshold and file the return. Every guard in this dictionary that refuses on this regime (interest:/interestReports/hasRequiredFactaFilings, form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/causesRetirementFactaFilingRequirementKO through its module's alias, and income's Schedule B Part III knockout) therefore reads Any(Not(this), above): an ASKED-and-unanswered filer is the permanent data-completeness residue and refuses; an answered-below filer files; an answered-above filer refuses because this dictionary does not produce Form 8938. FALSE on every committed return except the five form1099Rs facta fixtures that answer the attestation, which is the byte-identical argument.

Fact.Name: Above the Form 8938 reporting threshold (return level, complete safe)
Fact.Description: Whether the return's specified foreign financial assets exceed the Form 8938 reporting threshold that applies to it, the one answer every FATCA-shaped refusal in this dictionary reads. THREE ARMS, in order. (1) THE COMPUTED ARM, PREFERRED: when both aggregates and the filing status are answered, TRUE if the last-day total is MORE THAN /form8938ThresholdOnLastDayOfYear OR the maximum-during-the-year total is MORE THAN /form8938ThresholdAtAnyTimeDuringYear. Either figure alone satisfies the threshold; that is the printed rule and the Instructions' Example 3 (sold before year end, last day $0, maximum $125,000, "You have to file Form 8938") is its witness. (2) THE FALLBACK: form1099Rs:/writableSpecifiedForeignFinancialAssetsAboveForm8938Threshold, the filer's own yes/no statement, when the aggregates are not answered but that is. Kept rather than retired because the aggregates are new intake surface with no screen behind them yet, so a return that answered the old question would otherwise lose its answer. (3) FALSE when nothing was answered. THE PREDICATE IS A REAL ANSWERED-NESS TEST on the writables (/form8938AggregatesAnswered), never IsComplete on this fact or on its complete-safe siblings, which would always be true. WHAT THE ORDER MEANS FOR A FILER WHO ANSWERS BOTH: the figures win, on the form7206 line 2 precedent, because a yes/no that contradicts two stated dollar amounts is the less informative of the two answers; a consistency refusal was considered and not built, since the population is unreachable until a screen asks the aggregates. READ THIS FACT ONLY BESIDE /form8938ThresholdAnswered: arm (3) is "no answer", not "below", and a guard that reads this fact alone files a return the filer was never asked about. Arm (1) compares /form8938EffectiveLastDayValue and /form8938EffectiveMaximumValue rather than the two attested writables directly, and its guard /form8938AggregatesAnswered has a second route: a finished, valued Part V and Part VI inventory beside a known filing status. A filer who answers the attested figures is unaffected, figure for figure, because the attested route keeps its precedence inside the two effective facts. A filer who answers neither figure but completes the rows gets an answer through that route instead, in both directions: above the threshold it is refused for the reason named, and below it the three guards stop refusing it. WHAT ANSWERING TRUE MEANS: a Form 8938 must accompany the return and this dictionary does not produce one, so the return is refused, with the reason named.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 Part V: foreign deposit and custodial accounts, one row per account
Fact.Description: One row per foreign deposit or custodial account the filer (and, on a joint return, the spouse) has an interest in — the per-account detail Form 8938 Part V asks for and Part I totals. Each row is the source of one of the two Part I categories (deposit or custodial) and contributes its maximum value during the tax year to that category's Part I total; see /form8938ComputedNumberOfDepositAccounts and its three siblings for the roll-up. Building this collection turns the two Part I totals from a figure the filer computes by hand into one this dictionary can total for them, for the two categories this module builds; Part VI's other-asset rows are a separate collection. The row also carries line 22c, lines 24-25 currency details, and optional line 26b GIIN; these statement inputs do not affect Part I arithmetic.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 Part V account inventory is complete
Fact.Description: Whether the filer has finished entering every foreign deposit and custodial account for Part V. Yes with an empty collection is the explicit assertion that there are none. This is an intake control, not a printed tax fact; a successor must read it before treating the collection's Part I totals as final.

Fact.Name: Account type: custodial rather than deposit
Fact.Description: Whether this account is a CUSTODIAL account rather than a DEPOSIT account — the two boxes Form 8938 Part V line 20 offers ("a Deposit" / "b Custodial") for every account reported here. It decides which of the two Part I categories (deposit accounts, lines 5-6, or custodial accounts, lines 7-8) this row's count and value roll into.

Fact.Name: Account type: custodial rather than deposit (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The account-type answer read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, FALSE (deposit) when it was not. An unanswered type therefore counts the row toward the deposit category, never the custodial one, so an unanswered account cannot be silently dropped from both Part I totals.

Fact.Name: Financial institution in which the account is maintained
Fact.Description: The name of the financial institution in which this foreign deposit or custodial account is maintained, Form 8938 Part V line 26a. Identifying data for the statement itself; it does not feed any dollar total.

Fact.Name: Financial institution in which the account is maintained (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The institution name read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, an empty string when it was not. No consumer reads this today; exported so a successor fact or a print binding can take it without re-deriving the wrapper — the same wiring shape as ../isCustodialAccount and ../maximumValueDuringYear: measured against form1099Rs.xml's 41 per-item writables, only String fields ever carry Export, and even form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/writableAccountNumber — the fact this module's own account-number authority comment calls "the house pattern" — is NOT exported; its complete-safe twin is. This fact follows that precedent.

Fact.Name: Optional Part V line 26b global intermediary identification number
Fact.Description: The optional GIIN associated with the financial institution. Form 8938 permits this field to be left blank and gives no validation pattern; preserve the taxpayer-provided text without guessing a structural limit.

Fact.Name: Account number or other designation
Fact.Description: The account number, or other designation identifying the account, Form 8938 Part V line 21. Identifying data for the statement itself; it does not feed any dollar total.

Fact.Name: Account number or other designation (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The account number read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, an empty string when it was not. No consumer reads this today; exported for the same reason and on the same shape as ../financialInstitutionName.

Fact.Name: Mailing address of the financial institution (street)
Fact.Description: The mailing address of the financial institution in which this account is maintained — Form 8938 Part V line 27, "Number, street, and room or suite no.". A free text line on the printed form (not a structured domestic-style address block: the form prints line 27 and line 28 as two separate write-in lines, so this fact and ../writableInstitutionCityStateCountry are two String facts rather than one Address value). Identifying data for the statement itself; it does not feed any dollar total.

Fact.Name: Mailing address of the financial institution, street (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The street-address answer read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, an empty string when it was not. No consumer reads this today; exported on the same shape as ../financialInstitutionName.

Fact.Name: Mailing address of the financial institution (city, state/province, country, postal code)
Fact.Description: The city or town, state or province, country, and ZIP or foreign postal code of the financial institution's mailing address — Form 8938 Part V line 28, printed as one write-in line (see ../writableInstitutionMailingAddress for why this is a second String fact rather than a structured address). Identifying data for the statement itself; it does not feed any dollar total.

Fact.Name: Mailing address of the financial institution, city/state/country (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The city/state/country answer read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, an empty string when it was not. No consumer reads this today; exported on the same shape as ../financialInstitutionName.

Fact.Name: Account opened during the tax year
Fact.Description: Whether this account was opened during the tax year — Form 8938 Part V line 22a, one of the four "check all that apply" boxes. Identifying data for the statement itself; it does not feed any dollar total or any other fact in this module.

Fact.Name: Account opened during the tax year (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The line 22a answer read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, FALSE when it was not. No consumer reads this today; exported for the same reason as ../isCustodialAccount.

Fact.Name: Account closed during the tax year
Fact.Description: Whether this account was closed during the tax year — Form 8938 Part V line 22b. This is the per-account source of Part I line 9, "Were any foreign deposit or custodial accounts closed during the tax year?" (/form8938AnyDepositOrCustodialAccountClosedDuringYear): that return-level box is TRUE exactly when at least one account in this collection answers this line TRUE.

Fact.Name: Account closed during the tax year (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The line 22b answer read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, FALSE when it was not — so an unanswered account is treated as NOT closed for Part I line 9's purposes, the same direction every other complete-safe fact in this collection takes (an unanswered account contributes nothing rather than a false affirmative). Consumed by /form8938AnyDepositOrCustodialAccountClosedDuringYear.

Fact.Name: Account jointly owned with spouse
Fact.Description: Whether this Part V account is jointly owned with the spouse, Form 8938 line 22c. This is a printed checkbox only; it does not halve or otherwise change this account's maximum-value contribution.

Fact.Name: No tax item reported in Part III for this account
Fact.Description: Whether the filer did NOT report any tax item (interest, dividends, royalties, other income, gains/losses, deductions, credits) in Part III with respect to this account — Form 8938 Part V line 22d. Identifying data for the statement itself; it does not feed any dollar total or any other fact in this module (Part III itself is unbuilt — see the records overlay's FRONTIER-STATUS).

Fact.Name: No tax item reported in Part III for this account (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The line 22d answer read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, FALSE when it was not. No consumer reads this today; exported for the same reason as ../isCustodialAccount.

Fact.Name: Maximum value of this account during the tax year
Fact.Description: The highest value, in U.S. dollars, this ONE account reached at any time during the tax year — Form 8938 Part V line 23, the per-account figure Part I lines 6 and 8 total by category. Valued under the same printed rules as the return-level aggregates (see /writableForm8938MaximumValueDuringYear): fair market value, foreign currency converted to U.S. dollars, and an account with no positive value counts as zero (the Min 0 limit below is that floor). NO JOINT-OWNERSHIP HALVING APPLIES HERE, and that is correct rather than a gap: Part V's own line instructions say each spouse reports the account's FULL maximum value on their own separate Form 8938 ("You and your spouse each report the maximum value of an account held jointly by you and your spouse on your separate Forms 8938 filed with your separate income tax returns", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8938.pdf, "Spouses Filing Separate Returns", MIDDLE column of a THREE-column extraction, lines 1013/1015/1017/1019/1021/1023). The one-half rule belongs to a different quantity — the RETURN-LEVEL threshold aggregate (see /writableForm8938TotalValueOnLastDayOfYear), not this per-account figure. So every account is valued at its full answered figure, correctly. Optional: unanswered means this account's value was not asked or not yet entered.

Fact.Name: Maximum value of this account during the tax year (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The per-account maximum value read complete safely: the filer's answer when given, $0 when it was not, so an account added to this collection but not yet valued contributes nothing to either Part I total rather than leaving the total Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Part V line 24 foreign-currency conversion used
Fact.Description: Whether a foreign-currency exchange rate was used to convert this account's maximum value to U.S. dollars. If Yes, line 25 asks for the currency, rate, and (when the rate was not from Treasury) its source. The per-account maximum remains an entered U.S.- dollar value; this answer does not recompute it.

Fact.Name: Part V line 25a foreign currency
Fact.Description: The currency in which this account is maintained, when line 24 is Yes.

Fact.Name: Part V line 25b exchange rate as entered for printing
Fact.Description: The exchange rate used to convert this account's maximum value to U.S. dollars, preserved as entered. It is not a calculation input because line 23 is already the U.S.- dollar maximum.

Fact.Name: Part V line 25c helper: rate came from Treasury Fiscal Service
Fact.Description: Whether Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service provided the exchange rate. This helper distinguishes an intentionally blank source (Treasury rate) from a missing source when the filer used another rate.

Fact.Name: Part V line 25c non-Treasury exchange-rate source
Fact.Description: The source of the rate, when Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service did not provide it. Leave blank when the rate is from Treasury.

Fact.Name: Part V currency fields are conditionally complete (complete safe)
Fact.Description: TRUE when line 24 is answered No, or when it is Yes and lines 25a/25b and the Treasury-source answer are provided, plus line 25c's source when Treasury did not provide the rate. FALSE when a required answer is absent. The optional GIIN is not part of this test. This helper does not recompute the U.S.-dollar maximum or gate the current Part I roll-up; the collection-completion successor must consume it.

Fact.Name: Value of this account on the last day of the tax year
Fact.Description: What this ONE account was worth, in U.S. dollars, on the last day of the tax year. THIS IS NOT A PRINTED BOX. Form 8938 prints only a maximum value per row, but the reporting threshold is a two-operand test and its first operand is the total value on the last day of the year, so a threshold total derived from the rows needs a per-row year-end figure and the printed rows do not carry one. Valued under the same printed rules as the maximum beside it: fair market value, foreign currency converted to U.S. dollars, and an asset with no positive value counts as zero. Optional: unanswered means the year-end value was not asked or not yet entered, which leaves the computed threshold route unavailable and the return on whatever route it already had. It is deliberately outside the Part V and Part VI detail-completeness tests, so a return that answers only the printed boxes resolves exactly as it did before.

Fact.Name: This account is already reported on a form listed in Part IV
Fact.Description: Whether the filer reports this account on a Form 3520, 3520-A, 5471, 8621 or 8865 and therefore does not report it again on this statement. TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES TURN ON THIS ANSWER, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The asset leaves the STATEMENT: Part I and Part II count and total only what is reported in Part V and Part VI, and an excepted asset is reported on the other form instead, identified here only by the Part IV count of those forms. The asset stays in the THRESHOLD: a specified individual counts the value of an asset reported on one of those forms in deciding whether the reporting threshold is met. Optional and complete-safe: unanswered means not excepted, so a row entered before this question existed keeps the treatment it already had.

Fact.Name: This account is already reported on a form listed in Part IV (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The filer's answer when given, FALSE when it was not. Reading this rather than the writable keeps every row that predates the question on the statement, where it already was, instead of leaving the Part I and Part II roll-ups Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This row carries both figures the reporting threshold needs
Fact.Description: TRUE only when this row's maximum value during the year AND its value on the last day of the year are both answered. The threshold test has two operands and a row that answers one of them proves nothing about the other, so a total built from rows may only be read once every row answers both. FALSE, never Incomplete, when either is missing.

Fact.Name: This row enters the threshold total at one-half
Fact.Description: TRUE only when all three conditions hold together: the return is married filing separately, the filer has said the spouse is a specified individual, and this row is held jointly with that spouse. Two specified individuals who each file a separate annual return each include one-half of the value of an asset they own jointly. A joint owner who is a spouse but not a specified individual, or who is not a spouse at all, does not halve anything: each joint owner then includes the entire value. EVERY LEG IS ANSWERED-FIRST, so an unanswered filing status, an unanswered spouse question or an unanswered joint-ownership box leaves the row at its FULL value. That direction is deliberate: over-including can only make a return owe the form, never excuse it from owing one. THIS DOES NOT HALVE THE STATEMENT. Part I, Part II, Part V and Part VI report the asset at its full value on each spouse's own Form 8938; only the threshold total is halved.

Fact.Name: What this account adds to the last-day threshold total
Fact.Description: The year-end value this row contributes to the return-level last-day total: the answered figure, floored at zero in this body because a Min limit on a writable is not enforced when an answer is resolved, and halved when the one-half rule applies. $0 when the year-end value is unanswered, so the sum is never Incomplete; the inventory-complete test beside it, not this floor, is what keeps an unfinished inventory from being read as a total. An excepted asset still contributes here, because the threshold counts it.

Fact.Name: This asset's maximum value is more than the stated total for any time during the year
Fact.Description: TRUE when the stated any-time total of all specified foreign financial assets is answered and this asset's own maximum-value contribution is greater than it (floored at zero). FALSE when the stated total is unanswered or this asset's maximum is not greater.

Fact.Name: What this account adds to the any-time threshold total
Fact.Description: The maximum value this row contributes to the return-level any-time total, on the same three rules as the last-day contribution beside it: floored at zero in this body, halved when the one-half rule applies, $0 when the maximum is unanswered, and counted even when the asset is excepted from the statement.

The return-level `/form8938OtherAssetsIsDone` answer means the inventory is finished; until that and the required summary inputs are answered, the Part II outputs remain Incomplete. This collection does not yet feed the threshold aggregate, which is still the filer's own attested figure; wiring it would need the Part V accounts as well, and for a specified individual the threshold total INCLUDES assets reported on the Part IV forms (i8938 lines 369-375 and the CAUTION at 718-727), so no Part IV subtraction belongs in it .

Fact.Name: Part II summary inputs for this Part VI asset are complete
Fact.Description: True only when this asset's maximum value and its two Part II line 12 event answers are present, or, for a Part IV excepted asset (left out of the Part II summary), when its maximum value is present. An unanswered amount or event answer is not silently treated as zero or No when the summary is computed.

Fact.Name: Required Part VI fields for this asset are complete
Fact.Description: True when the description, identifying designation, two line-31 checkboxes, currency-use answer and line-35/36 branch are answered, with conditional dates and currency/entity/counterparty details present when applicable. Optional GIIN and a Treasury-provided rate source are not treated as missing. TRUE for a Part IV excepted asset (one reported on Form 3520, 3520-A, 5471, 8621 or 8865), which is not printed in Part VI and so owes no Part VI details. The additional line-36 inventory is IsComplete-first: if its new IsDone input is absent, this fact preserves the prior single-contact behavior; once answered, the explicit inventory must be complete.

Fact.Name: Value of this asset on the last day of the tax year
Fact.Description: What this ONE asset was worth, in U.S. dollars, on the last day of the tax year. THIS IS NOT A PRINTED BOX. Form 8938 prints only a maximum value per row, but the reporting threshold is a two-operand test and its first operand is the total value on the last day of the year, so a threshold total derived from the rows needs a per-row year-end figure and the printed rows do not carry one. Valued under the same printed rules as the maximum beside it: fair market value, foreign currency converted to U.S. dollars, and an asset with no positive value counts as zero. Optional: unanswered means the year-end value was not asked or not yet entered, which leaves the computed threshold route unavailable and the return on whatever route it already had. It is deliberately outside the Part V and Part VI detail-completeness tests, so a return that answers only the printed boxes resolves exactly as it did before.

Fact.Name: This asset is already reported on a form listed in Part IV
Fact.Description: Whether the filer reports this asset on a Form 3520, 3520-A, 5471, 8621 or 8865 and therefore does not report it again on this statement. TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES TURN ON THIS ANSWER, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The asset leaves the STATEMENT: Part I and Part II count and total only what is reported in Part V and Part VI, and an excepted asset is reported on the other form instead, identified here only by the Part IV count of those forms. The asset stays in the THRESHOLD: a specified individual counts the value of an asset reported on one of those forms in deciding whether the reporting threshold is met. Optional and complete-safe: unanswered means not excepted, so a row entered before this question existed keeps the treatment it already had.

Fact.Name: This asset is already reported on a form listed in Part IV (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The filer's answer when given, FALSE when it was not. Reading this rather than the writable keeps every row that predates the question on the statement, where it already was, instead of leaving the Part I and Part II roll-ups Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This row carries both figures the reporting threshold needs
Fact.Description: TRUE only when this row's maximum value during the year AND its value on the last day of the year are both answered. The threshold test has two operands and a row that answers one of them proves nothing about the other, so a total built from rows may only be read once every row answers both. FALSE, never Incomplete, when either is missing.

Fact.Name: This row enters the threshold total at one-half
Fact.Description: TRUE only when all three conditions hold together: the return is married filing separately, the filer has said the spouse is a specified individual, and this row is held jointly with that spouse. Two specified individuals who each file a separate annual return each include one-half of the value of an asset they own jointly. A joint owner who is a spouse but not a specified individual, or who is not a spouse at all, does not halve anything: each joint owner then includes the entire value. EVERY LEG IS ANSWERED-FIRST, so an unanswered filing status, an unanswered spouse question or an unanswered joint-ownership box leaves the row at its FULL value. That direction is deliberate: over-including can only make a return owe the form, never excuse it from owing one. THIS DOES NOT HALVE THE STATEMENT. Part I, Part II, Part V and Part VI report the asset at its full value on each spouse's own Form 8938; only the threshold total is halved.

Fact.Name: What this asset adds to the last-day threshold total
Fact.Description: The year-end value this row contributes to the return-level last-day total: the answered figure, floored at zero in this body because a Min limit on a writable is not enforced when an answer is resolved, and halved when the one-half rule applies. $0 when the year-end value is unanswered, so the sum is never Incomplete; the inventory-complete test beside it, not this floor, is what keeps an unfinished inventory from being read as a total. An excepted asset still contributes here, because the threshold counts it.

Fact.Name: This asset's maximum value is more than the stated total for any time during the year
Fact.Description: TRUE when the stated any-time total of all specified foreign financial assets is answered and this asset's own maximum-value contribution is greater than it (floored at zero). FALSE when the stated total is unanswered or this asset's maximum is not greater.

Fact.Name: What this asset adds to the any-time threshold total
Fact.Description: The maximum value this row contributes to the return-level any-time total, on the same three rules as the last-day contribution beside it: floored at zero in this body, halved when the one-half rule applies, $0 when the maximum is unanswered, and counted even when the asset is excepted from the statement.

Fact.Name: This asset's maximum value, counted only if it is reported on this statement
Fact.Description: ../writableMaximumValueDuringYear when this row is reported in Part VI, $0 when it is excepted because it is already reported on a form listed in Part IV. Part II line 11 totals the assets reported in Part VI, so an excepted asset contributes nothing to it. The same asset still contributes its full value to the reporting-threshold total through ../thresholdMaximumContribution, which is a different quantity.

Fact.Name: Part VI inventory and the Part II summary inputs are complete
Fact.Description: The inventory is complete only when the collection and explicit “done” answer are present and every item has its required Part VI details, amount and two event answers. Empty collection plus “done” is a complete zero; an unanswered collection, an unfinished inventory, or any incomplete row leaves the Part II totals Incomplete. For non-entity assets, the new additional-issuer IsDone answer is also IsComplete-first: when absent, the existing single-contact completeness behavior is preserved; once answered, the added statement inventory is required.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 Part II line 10 number of other foreign assets
Fact.Description: The number of Part VI assets, available only once the inventory and each row's summary inputs are complete.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 Part II line 11 maximum value of all Part VI assets
Fact.Description: The sum of the per-asset maximum values for the completed Part VI inventory. The threshold intake remains separate: it is the filer's attested return-level figure, and a specified individual counts the Part IV-reported assets in it too (i8938 lines 369-375 and the CAUTION at 718-727).

Fact.Name: Form 8938 Part II line 12 whether any other foreign asset was acquired or sold
Fact.Description: True when any Part VI asset was acquired or disposed of in the tax year; available only after the inventory and event answers are complete.

Fact.Name: The Part V account inventory is finished and every row carries both threshold figures
Fact.Description: TRUE only when the account collection was answered, the filer marked the inventory finished, and every row answers both its maximum value and its year-end value. An empty collection marked finished is a complete zero. An unanswered collection, an unfinished inventory, or one row missing either figure makes this FALSE, never Incomplete, so the return simply keeps whatever threshold route it already had. This is a narrower test than the Part V printed detail: it asks only for the two figures the threshold needs, so a filer who has not yet supplied an institution address is not blocked from the threshold answer. The printed statement has its own completeness residue, named in the contract.

Fact.Name: The Part VI asset inventory is finished and every row carries both threshold figures
Fact.Description: The Part VI counterpart of /form8938AccountThresholdInventoryComplete. It reuses the existing /form8938OtherAssetsIsComplete rather than restating it, and adds the one thing that test does not ask for: the per-row year-end value. FALSE, never Incomplete, whenever the inventory is unfinished or any row is missing a figure.

Fact.Name: Both asset inventories are finished and valued, and the filing status is known
Fact.Description: The single predicate that says the return's own asset rows may be read as the threshold totals. BOTH inventories must be finished, because a filer who lists foreign accounts and has not said whether there are other foreign assets has not answered the question the threshold asks; and the filing status must be known, because the threshold table is keyed on it and a computed total with no table to compare it against decides nothing. FALSE, never Incomplete, on every return that has not finished both.

Fact.Name: Part V accounts: total year-end value counted toward the reporting threshold
Fact.Description: The sum of every Part V row's year-end contribution, after the one-half rule and the zero floor, and including rows excepted from the statement because they are reported on a form listed in Part IV. Complete-safe: $0 when the collection was never answered, because a bare sum over an absent collection does not resolve and the return-level threshold facts above it must still say something. A $0 here is not a claim that the filer holds nothing; the inventory-complete test beside it is what decides whether this total may be read as the filer's answer.

Fact.Name: Part V accounts: total maximum value counted toward the reporting threshold
Fact.Description: The sum of every Part V row's maximum-value contribution, after the one-half rule and the zero floor, and including rows excepted from the statement. Complete-safe: $0 when the collection was never answered, because a bare sum over an absent collection does not resolve and the return-level threshold facts above it must still say something. A $0 here is not a claim that the filer holds nothing; the inventory-complete test beside it is what decides whether this total may be read as the filer's answer.

Fact.Name: Part VI assets: total year-end value counted toward the reporting threshold
Fact.Description: The sum of every Part VI row's year-end contribution, after the one-half rule and the zero floor, and including rows excepted from the statement. Complete-safe: $0 when the collection was never answered, because a bare sum over an absent collection does not resolve and the return-level threshold facts above it must still say something. A $0 here is not a claim that the filer holds nothing; the inventory-complete test beside it is what decides whether this total may be read as the filer's answer.

Fact.Name: Part VI assets: total maximum value counted toward the reporting threshold
Fact.Description: The sum of every Part VI row's maximum-value contribution, after the one-half rule and the zero floor, and including rows excepted from the statement. Complete-safe: $0 when the collection was never answered, because a bare sum over an absent collection does not resolve and the return-level threshold facts above it must still say something. A $0 here is not a claim that the filer holds nothing; the inventory-complete test beside it is what decides whether this total may be read as the filer's answer.

Fact.Name: Total value of specified foreign financial assets on the last day of the tax year, computed from the rows
Fact.Description: The last-day operand of the reporting-threshold test, computed from the return's own asset rows: the Part V total plus the Part VI total. Read it only beside /form8938ComputedInventoryComplete, which is what says the two inventories are finished; this fact alone resolves to $0 on a return that has entered nothing, and $0 is not an answer.

Fact.Name: Total value of specified foreign financial assets at any time during the tax year, computed from the rows
Fact.Description: The any-time operand of the reporting-threshold test, computed from the return's own asset rows: the Part V total plus the Part VI total. Each row carries its own maximum, and the maximums can fall on different days, so this sum is an upper bound on the total at any one time: it can say the any-time threshold is exceeded when the assets never reached it together, never the reverse. A filer in that position answers the any-time total directly (/writableForm8938MaximumValueDuringYear), which /form8938EffectiveMaximumValue reads first. Read it only beside /form8938ComputedInventoryComplete, which is what says the two inventories are finished; this fact alone resolves to $0 on a return that has entered nothing, and $0 is not an answer.

Fact.Name: Total value on the last day of the tax year, as the threshold test reads it
Fact.Description: The last-day figure the threshold test actually compares, chosen between the two routes that can supply it. ORDER, AND WHY. (1) THE ATTESTED FIGURE WINS whenever it is answered, floored at zero here because a Min limit on a writable is not enforced when an answer is resolved. That order preserves this module's own stated precedent that a figure the filer states directly outranks the other answer beside it, and it means no return that already answers the attested figures changes at all. It also stays on the safe side of the one thing the rows cannot know: the attested total is the filer's statement about ALL specified foreign financial assets, including any this dictionary's two inventories do not model. (2) THE ROWS, when the attested figure is not answered and both inventories are finished and valued. This is the new population: a filer who enters the statement rows and never sees the two return-level questions now has a threshold answer instead of a refusal. (3) NOTHING, when neither route is available, and this fact is then Incomplete by design. It is read only inside the arm of /form8938AboveReportingThreshold that /form8938AggregatesAnswered has already guarded, so that arm never fires without one of the two routes behind it. WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE: when both routes are answered and they DISAGREE, the attested figure wins silently and the disagreement is not refused, exactly as the module already leaves a yes/no that contradicts the stated figures unrefused. That is a named successor obligation, not a claim that the two can be trusted to agree.

(2) THE ROWS, when the attested figure is not answered and both inventories are finished and valued. (3) NOTHING, when neither route is available, and this fact is then Incomplete by design. It is read only inside the arm of /form8938AboveReportingThreshold that /form8938AggregatesAnswered has already guarded, so that arm never fires without one of the two routes behind it. WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE: when both routes are answered and they DISAGREE, the attested figure wins silently and the disagreement is not refused, exactly as the module already leaves a yes/no that contradicts the stated figures unrefused. That is a named successor obligation, not a claim that the two can be trusted to agree.

Fact.Name: All five Part IV form counts are answered
Fact.Description: True when the five existing counts are answered, including explicit zero. Unanswered counts are false. Counts are numbers of filed forms, not numbers of excepted assets.

Fact.Name: Part IV form counts need reconciliation review
Fact.Description: A nonblocking review signal. True when any answered count is negative, or an excepted asset was entered but the five form counts are not all answered or none is positive. Otherwise false. Several assets may be reported on one form; positive form counts without asset rows can be a valid Part-IV-only filing. False is not certification that every form is linked correctly.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 tax-item summary categories
Fact.Description: The fourteen printed categories in Part III: line 13 for deposit and custodial accounts and line 14 for other foreign assets, each with items a through g. These keys keep asset type separate from income type.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 Part III tax-item summary rows
Fact.Description: One disclosure-only row for each nonempty Part III tax-item category. Include only items attributable to assets actually reported in Parts V and VI, excluding Part IV excepted assets. An absent collection is unanswered. A finished empty collection means there are no such tax items; it is not an instruction to change income or tax.

Fact.Name: Form 8938 tax-item allocation is finished

Fact.Name: Form 8938 Part III line and item

Fact.Name: Amount already reported on the return for this tax-item category

Fact.Name: Form and line reporting this tax item
Fact.Description: The form number and line or lines where this category is already reported. Enter all locations, using a continuation statement when they cannot fit. An explicit empty string means no form location applies; unanswered remains incomplete. At least one of the two location cells must be nonempty, even for a zero-net reported item.

Fact.Name: Schedule and line reporting this tax item
Fact.Description: The schedule name and line or lines where this category is already reported. Enter all locations, using a continuation statement when they cannot fit. Fact.Name: Form 8938 summary row is complete
